evidence_summary: The pedal is documented as Made in USA; specialist historical research states Hohner did not make it in-house and the contractor remains unknown. Similar enclosure to Rogue Fuzz is treated only as a factory candidate, not proof of identity.
The Sound Modifier line is reported as third-party manufactured; individual models must be separated because country and builder evidence vary. No blanket German Hohner attribution should be made.

Echolette was the trade brand used for Klemt-made amplifiers and effect equipment; Klemt hand-built the equipment in Olching. Later Dynacord acquisition is retained as a separate ownership/manufacturing era.

Echolette was acquired by Dynacord in 1969; 1970s equipment was initially sold under both Echolette and Dynacord names, with brand production converging later. This is an ownership/production-era boundary, not evidence that every Echolette-labeled effect was newly designed by Dynacord.

A surviving 1970s Dynacord 5010 G listing documents an integrated fuzz/tremolo amplifier effect made in Germany. It is cataloged as an amp-integrated effect rather than a standalone stompbox and is not used to infer Dynacord stompbox production.

Klemt Echolette tape-echo units are documented as German-made and their preamps are associated with overdrive/fuzz-like saturation. Catalog only as effect-device context, not as a standalone fuzz pedal.
